## Appearance

Jane Andrews possesses an appearance that is described as neat, sensible, and plain.

_Sources: [v3 ch.Autumn P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004)_

## Personality

Jane Andrews is a steady, sensible, and unflappable individual who possesses a practical and lady-like demeanor. Described as plain, plodding, and conscientious, she excels at domestic science and cooking. Although she initially expressed a desire to devote her life to teaching without ever marrying, she eventually finds the profession monotonous.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. ## History

Jane Andrews attended school and Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) alongside [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Ruby Gillis](../character/ruby-gillis.md), during which she lived in the same boarding house as her [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) peers after starting classes at the academy. Prior to attending Queen's, she participated in a dramatic play of Elaine with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and Ruby. On one occasion, she traveled with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md) to a benefit concert at the [White Sands Hotel](../codex/places.md#white-sands-hotel), later sharing supper and a ride home with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md). Before her first term as a teacher, Jane met with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to discuss their different philosophies on teaching and discipline. She later resigned from the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school with plans to head West, eventually taking up a teaching position on the western prairies. Earlier in her youth, she joined [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md), and [Priscilla](../character/priscilla-grant.md) on a picnic walk where they discovered the garden of [Hester Gray](../character/hester-gray.md), and she accompanied [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) to unsuccessfully persuade [Judson Parker](../character/judson-parker.md) regarding fence advertisements. While staying overnight in Anne's room, Jane acted as a proxy to propose marriage to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) on behalf of her brother [Billy](../character/billy-andrews.md), leaving Jane somewhat offended when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) promptly rejected the offer.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P18](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0018), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P23](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0023), [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P31](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0031), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. The Hotel Concert P4](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0004), [v1 CHAPTER XXXIII. ## Quotes

> ““Of course it would be romantic,” conceded Jane Andrews, “but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)

> "The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 IV Different Opinions P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002)

> "Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever."
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIII A Golden Picnic P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)

> “I don’t know how you’re going to prevent him,” exclaimed Jane bitterly. “Everybody knows what Judson Parker is. He’d do anything for money. He hasn’t a spark of public spirit or any sense of the beautiful.”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v2 XIV A Danger Averted P41](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0041)

> “Oh, Anne,” gasped Jane, as they fled to the girls’ dressing room amid hearty cheers. “Oh, Anne I’m so proud! Isn’t it splendid?”
>
> — Jane Andrews — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream P8](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0008)
